extraction.name: ChartQA
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark for question answering about charts involving visual and logical reasoning. It covers 9,608 human-written questions and 23,111 questions generated from human-written chart summaries, spanning 20,882 charts collected from four real-world online sources.
extraction.creator: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, Enamul Hoque
extraction.citeAs: Ahmed Masry, Do Xuan Long, Jia Qing Tan, Shafiq Joty, and Enamul Hoque. 2022. ChartQA: A Benchmark for Question Answering about Charts with Visual and Logical Reasoning. arXiv:2203.10244 [cs.CL].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Charts were crawled from four different online sources: Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data (OWID), and Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD). For Pew, only chart images were crawled as underlying tables were unavailable. For Statista, OWID, and OECD, underlying data tables, metadata, SVG files, and associated text descriptions were extracted, and bounding box information was derived from the SVG files.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: For the Pew dataset, only chart images were crawled since the underlying data tables are not available.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Real-world chart images, underlying data tables, metadata (e.g., title, chart type), SVG files, and text descriptions crawled from Statista, Pew Research, Our World In Data, and OECD.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: To filter out invalid machine-generated questions, a heuristic was applied to filter out questions if the answer could not be found in the chart data table. Additionally, the test set of the machine-generated dataset was manually cleaned by removing invalid questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations were gathered via two procedures: (1) Human-authored QA pairs collected via Amazon Mechanical Turk, where crowdworkers wrote two questions (compositional and visual) with answers per chart, and another worker answered the same questions; and (2) Machine-generated QA pairs created from Statista human-written summaries using two fine-tuned T5 models (one for answer extraction and one for answer-aware question generation).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For human-authored QA pairs, exact match agreement between two crowd workers was 61.04%; when accounting for typos and lexical variations on 500 random samples, agreement reached 78.55%. Where annotator answers differed, manual checks were conducted to select the correct answer. For machine-generated QA, manual analysis of 1,250 pairs found 86.64% were complete, answerable, and correct given the chart.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk crowdworkers with an acceptance rate of 95% and at least 5,000 approved HITs, further filtered through a pre-test.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Models trained on the benchmark could potentially be abused to mislead the public regarding chart content and implications.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Automatic data extraction performance is lower on line, dot line, and pie charts; models struggle with nested mathematical/logical operations; current input representations separating data tables and visual features do not fully capture chart structure; and evaluation metrics for chart data extraction do not take textual tokens into consideration.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, validation, and testing of Chart Question Answering (ChartQA) models.
